papers.title: Fast, flexible analysis of differences in cellular composition with crumblr.
papers.abstract: Changes in cell type composition play an important role in human health and disease. Recent advances in single-cell technology have enabled the measurement of cell type composition at increasing cell lineage resolution across large cohorts of individuals. Yet this raises new challenges for statistical analysis of these compositional data to identify changes in cell type frequency. We introduce crumblr ( DiseaseNeurogenomics.github.io/crumblr ), a scalable statistical method for analyzing count ratio data using precision-weighted linear mixed models incorporating random effects for complex stud
papers.summary: The authors introduce crumblr, a scalable statistical method for analyzing cell type composition changes in single-cell data. It uses precision-weighted linear mixed models with random effects to handle complex study designs and count ratio data. This enables fast, flexible identification of cell type frequency differences across large cohorts.

papers.title: The spatiotemporal ecosystem of gallbladder cancer: From inflamed areas to invasive margins - Integrating biomechanical injury, the bile microenvironment, precursor lineages, and spatial niches.
papers.abstract: Gallbladder cancer (GBC) is usually described as the end point of chronic cholelithiasis-associated inflammation, and yet this linear formulation does not explain why only a small fraction of people with gallstones develop cancer, why histologically similar precursor lesions follow different evolutionary routes, or why invasion preferentially advances through anatomically and immunologically distinct interfaces. We propose a spatiotemporal ecosystem model that links five domains: gallstones and reflux as precipitating conditions; bile as a chemically active habitat; resident or transient micro
papers.summary: This review proposes a spatiotemporal ecosystem model for gallbladder cancer that integrates five interconnected domains: gallstones/reflux as precipitating conditions, bile as a chemically active habitat, precursor cell lineages, biomechanical injury, and spatially distinct immune niches. The authors argue that this framework better explains why only a fraction of gallstone patients develop cancer and why invasion progresses through specific anatomical interfaces than the traditional linear inflammation-to-cancer model.

papers.title: Multi-omic analysis of jaw-bone periosteum identifies the role of macrophage-derived SPP1 in Ctsk+Fmod+ periosteal cells.
papers.abstract: Periosteal cells (PCs) play a crucial role in bone regeneration. Currently, the spatial landscapes of jaw-bone periosteum during bone grafting remains unclear. In this study, we propose a modified guided bone regeneration (GBR) model and integrate single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) to dissect its spatial characteristics. We identify a functional subset of Ctsk+Fmod+ PCs within the jaw-bone periosteum of rat and human. In addition, we describe a spatial niche around the bone graft substitute, characterized by massive infiltration of macrophages interacting w
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to map the cellular landscape of jaw-bone periosteum during guided bone regeneration in a rat model. The authors identify a functional Ctsk+Fmod+ periosteal cell subset and show that macrophage-derived SPP1 signals to these cells within a spatial niche surrounding the bone graft substitute. This multi-omic atlas reveals key cell-cell interactions driving periosteal-mediated bone regeneration.

papers.title: OT-knn: A neighborhood-aware optimal transport framework for aligning spatial transcriptomics data.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) measures gene expression while preserving spatial context within tissues, enabling detailed characterization of tissue organization. As ST technologies advance, aligning datasets across tissue sections, individuals, platforms, and developmental stages has become increasingly important but remains challenging due to sparse expression, biological heterogeneity, and geometric distortions between slices. We introduce OT-knn, a method for ST alignment that integrates local neighborhood information within an optimal transport framework. Rather than relying solely on sing
papers.summary: OT-knn is a new computational method for aligning spatial transcriptomics datasets that incorporates local neighborhood information into an optimal transport framework. This approach addresses key challenges in spatial alignment, such as sparse gene expression, biological heterogeneity, and geometric distortions between tissue sections. The method aims to improve cross-section, cross-individual, and cross-platform comparisons in spatial transcriptomics studies.

papers.title: Spatially resolved multimodal hallmarks of response to neoadjuvant immunotherapies in the melanoma ecosystem in 2D and 3D.
papers.abstract: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy has transformed cancer treatment, yet the spatial molecular architecture governing response and resistance across distinct immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) regimens remains poorly defined. We assembled the largest neoadjuvant ICB (NICB) spatial multi-omics cohort to date, profiling over 112 million cells at single-cell resolution across three melanoma ICB regimens using MERFISH spatial transcriptomics, multiplexed immunofluorescence, and scRNA-sequencing. These analyses revealed the full multicellular spatial architecture of the NICB tumor microenvironment, including
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study assembled the largest neoadjuvant immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) spatial multi-omics cohort to date, profiling over 112 million cells across three melanoma ICB regimens using MERFISH spatial transcriptomics, multiplexed immunofluorescence, and scRNA-seq. It revealed the multicellular spatial architecture of the tumor microenvironment associated with response and resistance to neoadjuvant immunotherapy in melanoma.

papers.title: Integrating AI-Based Digital Pathology with Spatial Transcriptomics for Deeper Insight.
papers.abstract: Histopathology preserves tissue architecture, whereas spatial transcriptomics measures gene expression within its native spatial context. Integrating these modalities with artificial intelligence (AI) can link morphology to spatial molecular states and scale spatial discoveries to routine pathology cohorts. Early hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-to-spatial models demonstrated the feasibility of local gene-expression prediction. However, transcriptome-wide reconstruction remains constrained by gene-specific predictability, molecular sparsity, image quality, platform heterogeneity, and limited genera
papers.summary: This review discusses how combining AI-based digital pathology with spatial transcriptomics can link tissue morphology to spatial gene expression patterns, potentially scaling molecular discoveries to routine pathology cohorts. While early H&E-to-spatial models show feasibility for local gene prediction, transcriptome-wide reconstruction remains limited by gene-specific predictability, molecular sparsity, image quality, and platform heterogeneity.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses identify LMX1B as a tumor suppressor orchestrating the GDF15-ATP4B axis in renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is characterized by profound inter- and intratumoral heterogeneity and extensive tumor microenvironment (TME) remodeling, yet the spatially resolved cellular programs and intercellular communication networks orchestrating malignant progression remain poorly defined. LMX1B, a LIM homeodomain transcription factor essential for kidney morphogenesis, has not been previously investigated in renal carcinogenesis.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to map cellular programs and intercellular communication in renal cell carcinoma, identifying the transcription factor LMX1B as a tumor suppressor. LMX1B appears to act through a GDF15-ATP4B signaling axis, providing new insight into how this developmental regulator influences renal carcinogenesis.

papers.title: A Real-Data-Driven Framework for Evaluating Differential Transcript Usage Methods Across Long-Read Bulk, Single-Cell, and Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Differential transcript usage (DTU) analysis reveals transcript-level regulation in alternative splicing. With the rapid adoption of long-read sequencing in bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics, reliable evaluation of DTU methods under real biological conditions becomes essential. Current evaluation frameworks mainly rely on simulated data, which can introduce bias and may not reflect true regulatory mechanisms. A real-data-driven framework is constructed to evaluate DTU methods across long-read bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics. The framework includes two key components
papers.summary: This paper introduces a real-data-driven framework for benchmarking differential transcript usage (DTU) methods across long-read bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics. Unlike prior evaluations that rely mainly on simulated data, this framework uses real biological data to assess method performance, aiming to reduce bias and better reflect true regulatory mechanisms.

papers.title: Characterization of Resolved, Localized, and Progressing Infections at the Maternal-Fetal Interface in a Nonhuman Primate Model.
papers.abstract: Inflammation and infection are responsible for the majority of early preterm births. Host innate immune responses at the maternal-fetal interface that contribute to sterile intra-amniotic inflammation (SIAI), bacterial clearance, or invasive infection remain poorly understood. Group B Streptococcus ( Streptococcus agalactiae ) is a leading cause of preterm birth, stillbirth, and invasive neonatal disease.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study uses a nonhuman primate model to characterize how the maternal-fetal interface responds to Group B Streptococcus infection, distinguishing between resolved, localized, and progressing infections. It examines innate immune responses that lead to sterile intra-amniotic inflammation, bacterial clearance, or invasive infection, which are key drivers of early preterm birth.

papers.title: STCGCar: Graph Contrastive Learning with Reliable Augmentation for Spatial Transcriptomics Clustering.
papers.abstract: Accurately identifying spatial domains based on spatial transcriptomics (ST) data can greatly promote our understanding of cellular composition and tissue organization. While graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown significant advancements in spatial clustering, they tend to be insensitive to noisy edges, leading to intersections among identified spatial domains. Here, we introduce a GNN-based ST Clustering framework, called STCGCar, utilizing a Graph Contrastive learning model with reliable augmentation and redundancy reduction strategies. The framework begins by creating an enhanced view thr
papers.summary: STCGCar is a graph neural network framework for spatial transcriptomics clustering that uses graph contrastive learning with reliable augmentation and redundancy reduction to better identify spatial domains. It addresses the tendency of existing GNN methods to be insensitive to noisy edges, which causes spatial domains to overlap. The approach aims to improve the accuracy of tissue organization and cellular composition mapping from spatial transcriptomics data.

papers.title: Disentangling the cellular composition of FLCN-mutated tumors in Birt-Hogg-Dubé Syndrome by spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Birt-Hogg-Dubé (BHD) syndrome is a hereditary cancer predisposition syndrome caused by pathogenic variants in the folliculin (FLCN) gene and is associated with an increased risk of multifocal renal tumors. FLCN-mutated tumors (FMTs) often exhibit morphological heterogeneity with mixed morphological features resembling renal oncocytoma (RO) and chromophobe renal cell carcinoma (chRCC), yet the molecular basis underlying the heterogeneous morphologic features and the morphologic-genomic correlations remain poorly defined. In our prior work, we identified mutually exclusive expressions of L1 cell
papers.journal: Modern pathology : an official journal of the United States and Canadian Academy of Pathology, Inc
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics to dissect the cellular composition of FLCN-mutated renal tumors in Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome, which often show mixed features resembling oncocytoma and chromophobe RCC. The authors aim to link the morphological heterogeneity of these tumors to their underlying molecular and genomic profiles, building on prior findings of mutually exclusive L1 cell adhesion molecule expression.

papers.title: Machine learning-based identification of core regulatory targets in 1-nitropyrene-induced placental trophoblast dysfunction and FGR.
papers.abstract: 1-NP (1-Nitropyrene), a nitrated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon derived from diesel combustion, is a widespread environmental pollutant with potential reproductive toxicity. However, its role in FGR (fetal growth restriction) and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Our in vivo results revealed that 1-NP exposure leads to FGR and placental damage in mice, marked by reduced fetal and placental weights, and altered labyrinthine morphology. Integration of scRNA-seq (single-cell RNA sequencing) and bulk RNA-seq data using the Scissor algorithm identified EVTs (extravillous trophoblasts) as t
papers.summary: This study shows that exposure to 1-nitropyrene, a diesel exhaust pollutant, causes fetal growth restriction and placental damage in mice. By combining single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing with a machine learning algorithm (Scissor), the authors pinpoint extravillous trophoblasts as the key cell type affected and identify core regulatory targets driving this placental dysfunction.

papers.title: Cell-type-specific circadian and light-responsive transcriptional dynamics in adult Drosophila neurons.
papers.abstract: The Drosophila adult central brain contains 240 circadian neurons, of which there are more than 25 different neuron subtypes based on connectomic data. Recent single-cell RNA-seq characterization of these neurons "around the clock" also indicates a similar number of molecular subtypes of circadian neurons, but other conclusions from these transcriptomic studies warranted verifying and extending with other approaches. To address these limitations, we used three complementary approaches: 1) We used a genetic multiplexing strategy to profile the transcriptomes of circadian neurons from multiple t
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: This study uses a genetic multiplexing strategy to profile transcriptomes of circadian neurons in the adult Drosophila brain, revealing cell-type-specific circadian and light-responsive transcriptional dynamics. It verifies and extends prior single-cell RNA-seq findings by characterizing molecular subtypes of circadian neurons with complementary approaches.

papers.title: Layer-Resolved Spatial Transcriptomic Profiling Reveals Distinct Fibrotic and Muscularizing Submucosal Niches in Fibrostenotic Crohn's Disease.
papers.abstract: Fibrostenotic stricture is a severe complication of Crohn's disease (CD) that affect up to 50% of patients over their lifetime, causing irreversible narrowing of the intestinal lumen and bowel obstruction, but the molecular programs that distinguish stenotic from non-stenotic inflammation and the relative contributions of fibrosis and smooth-muscle remodeling remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to dissect bowel-wall compartment-specific and histology-defined remodeling programs in fibrostenotic CD.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study uses layer-resolved spatial transcriptomics to profile the bowel wall in fibrostenotic Crohn's disease, distinguishing molecular programs in stenotic versus non-stenotic inflamed tissue. The authors identify distinct fibrotic and muscularizing submucosal niches, suggesting that fibrosis and smooth-muscle remodeling are separable processes within the stricture microenvironment.

papers.title: Spatial and single-cell dissection of medulloblastoma identifies developmental hierarchies and a prognostic PPIA-BSG tumor-immune axis.
papers.abstract: Medulloblastoma (MB) in children is highly heterogeneous, leading to its classification into molecular subgroups and resulting in significant differences in clinical outcomes even within the same risk group. This heterogeneity severely hampers the clinical management of MB. Therefore, it is essential to characterize MB heterogeneity within its tumor microenvironment.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial and single-cell transcriptomics to dissect the tumor microenvironment of pediatric medulloblastoma, revealing developmental hierarchies within tumor cell populations. The authors identify a PPIA-BSG tumor-immune axis that correlates with patient prognosis, offering a potential biomarker and therapeutic target.

papers.title: Longitudinal single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveals intratumor heterogeneity, therapeutic response, and comparative value of canine marginal zone lymphoma.
papers.abstract: Diffuse B-cell lymphomas are the most prevalent canine hematologic malignancies, and their clinical presentation resembles that of human B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas (NHLs). However, a lack of a clear subtyping framework perpetuates imprecise treatment approaches that fail to address mechanisms of therapy resistance. Here, we employed deep phenotyping via serial sampling and longitudinal transcriptomics to evaluate intratumoral composition and therapy response in a 6-year-old neutered male goldendoodle with stage 5A marginal zone lymphoma (MZL). Following sequential treatment consisting of a s
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study uses longitudinal single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to deeply characterize intratumor heterogeneity and therapeutic response in a single dog with marginal zone lymphoma, a spontaneous B-cell malignancy that mirrors human non-Hodgkin lymphoma. By serially sampling the tumor over the course of treatment, the authors track how distinct cell populations and spatial niches evolve under therapy, offering a comparative framework for understanding therapy resistance. The work highlights the potential of canine lymphomas as a translational model for human disease.

papers.title: An eicosanoid-enriched follicular microenvironment shapes germinal centre immune dynamics in antiretroviral-treated PLWH.
papers.abstract: Delineating the follicular (F) cellular and molecular landscape in HIV infection is essential for understanding neutralizing antibody responses and HIV reservoir maintenance. Multiplex imaging analysis revealed a less differentiated profile for follicular helper CD4 T cells (T FH ) and significantly increased follicular CD25 lo/hi Foxp3 hi T cells in lymph nodes (LNs) from antiretroviral treated (cART) compared to viremic (Vir) people living with HIV (PLWH). Spatial transcriptomics identified distinct inflammatory follicular microenvironments in Vir and cART LNs, characterized by interferon an
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study maps the follicular immune landscape in lymph nodes of people living with HIV, comparing those on antiretroviral therapy (cART) to viremic individuals. Using multiplex imaging and spatial transcriptomics, the authors found that cART-treated lymph nodes show less differentiated follicular helper T cells and increased regulatory T cells, along with distinct inflammatory microenvironments enriched in eicosanoids that shape germinal centre dynamics.

papers.title: Microenvironmental and transcriptional determinants of the robustness of spinal cord regeneration in zebrafish.
papers.abstract: Unlike mammals, adult zebrafish can regenerate spinal cord tissue after complete transection. We report here that a substantial proportion of zebrafish receiving this injury fail to regain locomotor function, and we analyzed this critically. After stratifying large cohorts of injured animals according to functional recovery, we directly compared recovered and non-recovered individuals at matched post-injury stages. We find that permanently paralyzed animals form a tissue bridge across the lesion yet exhibit impaired axonal invasion and regrowth to downstream targets. Integrative single-nucleus
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study shows that spinal cord regeneration in zebrafish is not universally successful: a substantial fraction of injured fish fail to recover locomotor function despite forming a tissue bridge across the lesion. By comparing recovered and non-recovered individuals at matched post-injury stages, the authors identify impaired axonal invasion and regrowth as key determinants of failed regeneration, using integrative single-nucleus approaches to link microenvironmental and transcriptional factors to recovery outcomes.

papers.title: Disentangling covariate effects on single-cell-resolved epigenomes with DeepDive.
papers.abstract: Understanding the effects of individual biological factors from single-cell-resolved epigenomic data is hindered by multicollinearity, particularly in human cohorts. We introduce DeepDive, a deep-learning framework designed to systematically disentangle known and unknown sources of variation in single-nucleus ATAC-seq data. DeepDive accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms state-of-the-art methods with incomplete covariate information, and robustly recovers true biological signals from even highly entangled covariates, unlocking counterfactual, "what-if," analyses. Applying
papers.summary: DeepDive is a deep-learning framework that disentangles the effects of individual biological factors from single-nucleus ATAC-seq data, addressing the problem of multicollinearity in human cohort studies. It accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms existing methods when covariate information is incomplete, and enables counterfactual 'what-if' analyses by recovering true biological signals from entangled covariates.

papers.title: OscillomeR infers ultradian oscillations and targets of the Hes family.
papers.abstract: The Hes family, basic-helix-loop-helix transcription factors and downstream effectors of Notch signaling, regulate the fate choices of pancreatic progenitors, muscle stem cells, neuronal progenitors, and presomitic mesoderm cells. Bioluminescence imaging (BLI) has revealed ultradian oscillatory dynamics of Hes-family members Hes1, Hes5, and Hes7. However, identifying which of the Hes target genes also oscillate remains challenging due to the time-consuming and costly nature of tracking individual target genes using BLI. Here, we propose OscillomeR, a computational framework that reconstructs u
papers.summary: OscillomeR is a computational framework that infers ultradian oscillatory dynamics of Hes-family transcription factors and predicts which of their target genes also oscillate, bypassing the need for costly bioluminescence imaging of each gene. This enables systematic identification of oscillating targets in Notch signaling contexts such as pancreatic, muscle, and neuronal progenitors.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: This paper introduces a meta-classifier that arbitrates disagreements between gene regulatory network inference methods on a per-edge basis, rather than selecting one method or averaging all of them. A gradient-boosted model is trained on the raw scores from ten inference methods (including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR, and ARACNe) to weight each method differently for each candidate regulator-target pair, and the authors also propose a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts. The approach is evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens.

papers.title: Integration of Single-Cell and Bulk RNA Sequencing Data to Identify Lactylation-Related Gene Signatures in Hepatic Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury Using Machine Learning Algorithms.
papers.abstract: Hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (HIRI) is not only a common complication of liver transplantation and major hepatic surgery but also a critical determinant of postoperative prognosis. Lactate metabolic reprogramming has been observed in HIRI, yet the role of lactate and its related lactylation in the pathogenesis of HIRI remains unclear. To address this, we integrated single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data with multiple bioinformatic approaches. Five single-cell gene set activity scoring methods (AUCell, UCell, singscore, ssGSEA, and AddModuleScore) were applied to evaluate lactylation activity
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing data to investigate lactylation-related gene signatures in hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (HIRI). Using five gene set activity scoring methods and machine learning algorithms, the authors identify lactylation-associated genes that may contribute to HIRI pathogenesis. The findings suggest lactate metabolism and lactylation play a role in HIRI and could serve as potential biomarkers or therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis reveals an epithelial cell-derived prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature with ADAM12 as a key functional regulator in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: This study developed a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for NSCLC using single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data. By integrating TCGA and GEO datasets with machine learning, we identified key epithelial cells-related genes predictive of immunotherapy response. PIS effectively stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS individuals showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. We confirmed the high expression of ADAM12 in both tissue samples and cell lines, and validated its functional roles through cellular assays. Furthermore, mouse model experiments d
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data to build a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for non-small cell lung cancer, based on epithelial cell-derived genes. The signature stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, and the authors validate ADAM12 as a key functional regulator through cell line and mouse experiments.

papers.title: Machine learning identifies ac4C-related prognostic signature and TUBA1C as therapeutic target in COAD.
papers.abstract: To explore the role of N4-acetylcytidine (ac4C)-related genes (acRGs) in colon adenocarcinoma (COAD) and identify reliable prognostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets. Multi-source transcriptomic datasets (TCGA-COAD, GSE39582, GSE17536) and single-cell RNA-seq data were analyzed. Ten machine learning algorithms were integrated to construct an acRG-based prognostic signature (acRGBS). Immune microenvironment (TME) and genomic profiling were performed, with in vitro functional experiments validating TUBA1C's role. acRGBS, comprising four hub genes (SARAF, CDC42SE2, TSPYL2, TUBA1C), e
papers.journal: Mammalian genome : official journal of the International Mammalian Genome Society
papers.summary: This study used multi-source transcriptomic and single-cell data with ten machine learning algorithms to build an ac4C-related gene prognostic signature (acRGBS) for colon adenocarcinoma, identifying four hub genes including TUBA1C. In vitro experiments validated TUBA1C as a potential therapeutic target, and the signature was linked to immune microenvironment and genomic features.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and machine learning analysis identifies a tumor doubling time-related prognostic signature and therapeutic targets in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) exhibits marked molecular heterogeneity and diverse clinical outcomes, partly influenced by HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment. Although tumor doubling time (TDT) reflects tumor growth kinetics and has prognostic relevance, its molecular basis in HNSCC remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing with machine learning to identify a gene signature associated with tumor doubling time (TDT) in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. The authors link this TDT-related signature to prognosis and propose potential therapeutic targets, while accounting for HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment.

papers.title: A systematic benchmark of bioinformatics methods for single-cell and spatial RNA-seq nanopore long reads data.
papers.abstract: Alternative splicing plays a crucial role in transcriptomic complexity, yet remains difficult to resolve at the single-cell level due to the limitations of short-read technologies. Coupling single-cell with long-read sequencing offers full-length transcript coverage, enabling more accurate isoform detection. Diverse computational tools tailored for single-cell and spatial long-read transcriptomics have been developed. To compare the effectiveness of these approaches, we generated paired short-read and Nanopore long-read single-cell datasets, tailored for benchmarking bioinformatics tools. We e
papers.summary: This paper presents a systematic benchmark of computational tools for analyzing single-cell and spatial RNA-seq data generated with Nanopore long-read sequencing. The authors created paired short-read and long-read single-cell datasets to evaluate how well different bioinformatics methods detect full-length transcripts and alternative splicing isoforms. The study provides guidance on tool selection for researchers working with long-read single-cell transcriptomics.

papers.title: Interpretable multi-omics integration across mixed-order tensors with MANTRA.
papers.abstract: The integration of multi-modal molecular data is crucial for understanding complex diseases, but existing methods struggle with modern experimental designs that generate datasets with mixed-order tensors-for example, a third-order drug-response tensor alongside a second-order transcriptomics matrix. Here, we present MANTRA (Multi-view ANalysis with Tensor and matRix Alignment), a probabilistic framework that integrates collections of tensors of different orders, combining the strengths of group factor analysis and tensor decomposition. MANTRA learns interpretable latent factors and naturally h
papers.summary: MANTRA is a probabilistic framework that integrates multi-omics datasets of different tensor orders (e.g., third-order drug-response tensors and second-order transcriptomics matrices) by combining group factor analysis with tensor decomposition. It learns interpretable latent factors, addressing a gap in existing methods that cannot handle mixed-order tensor designs common in modern experiments.

papers.title: Alignment-free integration of single-nucleus ATAC-seq across species with sPYce.
papers.abstract: Changes in gene regulation largely contribute to differences in cellular identities and phenotypes between species. Single-nucleus assays for transposase-accessible chromatin with sequencing (snATAC-seq) are an efficient strategy to identify putative gene regulatory elements and provide new insight into evolutionary divergence of regulatory programmes. However, no dedicated framework exists to integrate and compare snATAC-seq data across species, while methods designed for single-cell gene expression data have serious limitations. Here we present sPYce, a cross-species snATAC-seq integration m
papers.summary: The authors present sPYce, a new computational framework for integrating single-nucleus ATAC-seq data across species without requiring sequence alignment. This addresses a gap in cross-species regulatory comparison, since existing single-cell integration methods designed for gene expression data perform poorly on chromatin accessibility data. sPYce enables identification of conserved and divergent gene regulatory elements between species.

papers.title: COL1A1+ Epithelial Cells Orchestrate VEGFA-VEGFR Signaling in Endometritis Revealed by Single-Cell Analysis.
papers.abstract: Endometritis is linked to adverse reproductive outcomes, but epithelial programs in disease initiation and persistence remain unclear. We aimed to systematically define inflammation-associated epithelial states and regulation in endometritis using single-cell analysis.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell analysis to identify inflammation-associated epithelial cell states in endometritis, highlighting COL1A1+ epithelial cells as key orchestrators of VEGFA-VEGFR signaling. The findings suggest these cells may drive disease initiation and persistence, offering potential targets for understanding and treating endometritis.

papers.title: microRNAs as Regulators of the Immune Response and Their Potential Therapeutic Applications in Cancer.
papers.abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are small non-coding RNAs that have emerged as critical regulators of gene expression and key cellular processes in cancer, including tumor cell proliferation, survival, metastasis, and both innate and adaptive immune responses within the tumor microenvironment. Through their ability to modulate immune cell development, differentiation, polarization, antigen presentation, cytokine signaling and immune checkpoint expression, miRNAs play a vital role in shaping immune responses and represent attractive therapeutic candidates for remodeling the tumor immune microenvironment. Th
papers.summary: This review discusses how microRNAs regulate both innate and adaptive immune responses within the tumor microenvironment, influencing immune cell development, polarization, antigen presentation, and immune checkpoint expression. It highlights the therapeutic potential of targeting miRNAs to remodel the tumor immune microenvironment in cancer treatment.

papers.title: High-resolution spatial transcriptomics of irradiated submandibular glands treated with fortified fibrin hydrogels.
papers.abstract: Previous studies showed that fortified fibrin hydrogel (Ep-FH), generated by conjugating laminin-1 peptides (A99 and YIGSR) and growth factors (FGF7 and FGF10) to fibrin hydrogels, improves epithelial organization and secretory function in irradiated mouse submandibular glands (SMG). To define the cell type-specific mechanisms underlying these effects, we generated high-resolution spatial transcriptomic profiles using the Xenium Prime Mouse Pan Tissue and Pathways Panel (5,000 genes). Treatment with Ep-FH partially reactivated secretory- and polarity-related genes, shifted stromal and immune t
papers.summary: This study uses high-resolution spatial transcriptomics (Xenium Prime Mouse Pan Tissue and Pathways Panel, 5,000 genes) to dissect how fortified fibrin hydrogels (Ep-FH) improve epithelial organization and secretory function in irradiated mouse submandibular glands. The treatment partially reactivated secretory- and polarity-related genes and shifted stromal and immune cell populations, revealing cell type-specific mechanisms underlying gland recovery.

papers.title: Combined multi-omics profiling and machine learning analysis reveals that Bregs and RPS2 promote bone metastasis in nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
papers.abstract: The bone is the primary site of distant metastasis in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), and bone metastasis (BM) significantly increases mortality. Deciphering the complex crosstalk between cancer cells and their tumor microenvironment (TME) is crucial for identifying therapeutic targets aimed at eliminating metastasis-initiating cells and preventing the establishment of overt metastases. Regulatory B cells (Bregs), a specialized B-cell subset endowed with potent immunosuppressive functions, play a pivotal regulatory role within the TME. However, their specific contributions, pheno
papers.summary: This study combines multi-omics profiling with machine learning to investigate how regulatory B cells (Bregs) and the ribosomal protein RPS2 contribute to bone metastasis in nasopharyngeal carcinoma. The authors identify Bregs and RPS2 as potential drivers of the metastatic process, suggesting they may serve as therapeutic targets to prevent bone metastasis.

papers.title: STC1 is associated with tumor progression and suppressive niches in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) exhibits high recurrence and therapy resistance. We aimed to investigate the undefined role of Stanniocalcin-1 (STC1) in LSCC pathogenesis.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of Stanniocalcin-1 (STC1) in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC), a cancer with high recurrence and therapy resistance. The authors associate STC1 expression with tumor progression and immunosuppressive niches, suggesting it may contribute to LSCC pathogenesis and serve as a potential target.

papers.title: Diurnal Insulin Clearance and Circadian Metabolic Gene Signatures in MASLD: Integrative Multi-Dataset Physiological and Transcriptomic Analysis.
papers.abstract: Insulin clearance is a key determinant of circulating insulin availability, but its diurnal variation and relationship with circadian metabolic programs in metabolic dysfunction associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remain unclear. This study aimed to explore diurnal insulin clearance in humans and examine associated metabolic gene signatures in MASLD.
papers.summary: This study investigates how insulin clearance varies across the day in humans and whether this diurnal pattern is linked to circadian metabolic gene expression programs in MASLD. By integrating physiological and transcriptomic datasets, the authors identify associations between time-of-day insulin clearance and circadian metabolic gene signatures in steatotic liver disease.

papers.title: scLTF: A self-training clustering framework for large-scale single-cell RNA-Seq data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology has rapidly advanced in recent years, driving significant breakthroughs in developmental biology, cancer research, immunology, and other related fields. However, existing clustering methods still face performance bottlenecks when handling large-scale scRNA-seq data. To address this challenge, we propose a self-training clustering method for large-scale single-cell RNA-seq data, termed scLTF (Single-cell Louvain-Transformer Framework for Large-scale Clustering). This method first generates preliminary clusters using a fast Louvain algorithm and
papers.summary: scLTF is a self-training clustering framework for large-scale scRNA-seq data that combines a fast Louvain algorithm for initial clustering with a Transformer-based model to refine cluster assignments. The approach aims to overcome performance bottlenecks of existing clustering methods when applied to large datasets.

papers.title: Single-cell-informed senescence programs underpin a machine-learning prognostic model robustly validated across melanoma cohorts.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence (CS) shapes tumor evolution and the tumor microenvironment (TME), yet senescence-informed prognostic models for skin cutaneous melanoma (SKCM) remain limited. We aimed to develop and validate a robust senescence-related prognostic signature by integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data with systematic machine-learning screening.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to identify cellular senescence programs in skin cutaneous melanoma and uses machine-learning screening to build a senescence-related prognostic signature. The resulting model is validated across multiple independent melanoma cohorts, suggesting senescence-informed signatures can robustly stratify patient outcomes.

papers.title: Multi-omics and machine learning reveal LYZ and ISG15 as diagnostic and therapeutic targets in autoimmune-mediated chronic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: CKD represents a substantial worldwide health challenge, defined by the gradual development of tubulointerstitial fibrosis and reduced renal performance. Autoimmune-mediated factors are central to this pathological process, yet early diagnostic biomarkers and specific therapeutic targets are scarce. The objective of this research is to systematically pinpoint crucial specific genes that contribute to autoimmune-mediated CKD progression.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with machine learning to identify LYZ and ISG15 as key genes involved in autoimmune-mediated chronic kidney disease. The authors propose these genes as potential diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets, addressing the current scarcity of early markers for this condition.

papers.title: Identification and Validation of a Two-Gene NK Cell-Related Risk Model for COPD: Integration of Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Analysis.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) involves chronic inflammation with potential involvement of natural killer (NK) cells, but NK cell-related diagnostic markers remain limited. This study aimed to identify NK cell-related hub genes and construct a risk model for COPD.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data to identify natural killer (NK) cell-related hub genes in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and builds a two-gene risk model for diagnosis. The authors validate this model as a potential tool for distinguishing COPD patients, highlighting NK cell involvement in disease pathogenesis.

papers.title: Progress and challenges in exploring the pathogenesis of depressive disorders via RNA sequencing.
papers.abstract: Depressive disorders (DD) are highly heterogeneous psychiatric illnesses. Their complex pathogenesis, coupled with suboptimal response rates to current clinical treatments, poses significant challenges to global mental health. High-throughput RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) has emerged as a powerful tool for dissecting the molecular mechanisms of DD at the transcriptomic level. This paper reviews recent advances utilizing bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq), and single-nucleus RNA-seq (snRNA-seq) to explore the pathogenesis of major depressive disorder (MDD), perinatal depression (PND), per
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent progress in using bulk, single-cell, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing to investigate the molecular pathogenesis of depressive disorders, including major depressive disorder and perinatal depression. It highlights how transcriptomic approaches are revealing cellular and molecular heterogeneity underlying these conditions, while also discussing remaining technical and analytical challenges.

papers.title: Single-cell Raman profiling of B cell differentiation and leukemic transformation with transcriptome inference.
papers.abstract: Label-free profiling of cellular transcriptional and metabolic states during B cell differentiation and malignant transformation remains technically challenging. Raman spectroscopy offers a non-destructive alternative for single-cell biochemical characterization, yet its ability to infer transcriptomic profiles and distinguish leukemic cells has been limited.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell Raman spectroscopy to profile B cell differentiation and leukemic transformation in a label-free, non-destructive manner, and develops a method to infer transcriptomic states from Raman spectral data. The approach aims to distinguish leukemic cells from normal differentiating B cells based on their biochemical signatures.

papers.title: From transcriptomic profiling to precision oncology: a bibliometric analysis of RNA sequencing in acute myeloid leukemia.
papers.abstract: RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) has become an important tool for investigating the molecular heterogeneity of acute myeloid leukemia (AML); however, the global development and thematic evolution of this field remain inadequately characterized.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis maps the global research landscape of RNA sequencing in acute myeloid leukemia, examining publication trends, key contributors, and thematic evolution over time. It characterizes how transcriptomic profiling has increasingly been linked to precision oncology applications in AML, though the abstract provides limited detail on specific findings.

papers.title: Peripheral blood cells and immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis: a retrospective clinical study with pharmacovigilance and single-cell analysis.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated myocarditis (ICI-M) is a rare but potentially lethal immune-related adverse event (irAE). Early identification of fulminant (severe) cases remains challenging, and the peripheral immune derangements underlying ICI-M are incompletely characterized.
papers.summary: This retrospective clinical study investigates immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI-M), a rare but potentially fatal side effect of cancer immunotherapy, using pharmacovigilance data and single-cell analysis of peripheral blood cells. The authors aim to identify early markers of severe (fulminant) cases and characterize the immune cell changes in the blood that accompany this condition.

papers.title: Multi-omics mapping of PSC genetic risk to a high TWAS-active JAML+ lipid-associated macrophage program: bridging single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niches, and machine learning selection.
papers.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease with progressive peribiliary inflammation and fibrosis. Disease-modifying therapies are lacking, and the cell-type-specific mechanisms linking genetic susceptibility to pathogenic immune states remain incompletely understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to map primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) genetic risk variants to a specific immune cell program—JAML+ lipid-associated macrophages—that shows high transcriptome-wide association activity. By combining single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niche mapping, and machine learning, the authors link genetic susceptibility to a pathogenic macrophage state in the diseased liver. The work provides a framework for identifying cell-type-specific therapeutic targets in PSC.

papers.title: Identification and experimental validation of CCL26 as a core comorbid gene and biomarker for atopic dermatitis and allergic asthma via machine learning and multi-omics analysis.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) and allergic asthma (AA) frequently co-occur and are a core component of the "atopic march." However, the shared molecular mechanisms linking these conditions, as well as the core comorbid genes with diagnostic value, remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning and multi-omics analysis to identify CCL26 as a shared core gene and potential biomarker linking atopic dermatitis and allergic asthma, two conditions that frequently co-occur in the 'atopic march.' The authors experimentally validate CCL26, suggesting it may serve as a diagnostic marker and therapeutic target for these comorbid allergic diseases.

papers.title: Genetic associations link lung cancer liability to brain imaging phenotypes and nominate an FN1-associated tumor-oligodendrocyte program in small-cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: Brain metastasis is a major cause of mortality in lung cancer, particularly in small-cell lung cancer (SCLC). Whether genetic susceptibility to lung cancer is associated with brain structural and functional traits relevant to metastatic vulnerability remains unclear. We investigated subtype-specific genetic associations with brain imaging phenotypes and explored the biological context of the SCLC-associated white-matter signal.
papers.summary: This study uses genetic correlation and Mendelian randomization-style analyses to link lung cancer liability, especially small-cell lung cancer (SCLC), to brain imaging phenotypes such as white-matter microstructure. The authors then nominate an FN1-associated tumor-oligodendrocyte program that may underlie SCLC brain metastatic vulnerability. The work connects cancer genetics with neuroimaging and proposes a candidate cellular mechanism for brain metastasis.

papers.title: Circulating and tumor-infiltrating immune cell profiles in cervical cancer checkpoint blockade: multi-omics biomarkers of response and resistance.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has changed the therapeutic landscape of cervical cancer, but clinical benefit remains heterogeneous and difficult to predict with single biomarkers. Cervical cancer is a particularly suitable setting for immune-cell profiling because HPV-driven antigenicity, chemoradiotherapy-induced tissue remodeling, anti-angiogenic combinations, and repeated exposure to PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors all shape the blood-tumor immune axis. This Mini Review discusses how circulating immune cells and tumor-infiltrating immune cells can be jointly interrogated by multi-omics technologies to i
papers.summary: This mini review discusses how combining circulating immune cell profiling with tumor-infiltrating immune cell analysis via multi-omics can identify biomarkers predicting response or resistance to immune checkpoint blockade in cervical cancer. It highlights that HPV-driven antigenicity, chemoradiotherapy, anti-angiogenic combinations, and prior PD-1/PD-L1 exposure all shape the blood-tumor immune axis, making single biomarkers insufficient. The authors argue that integrated multi-omics immune profiling is needed to stratify patients for checkpoint inhibitor therapy.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence for automated detection of interictal epileptiform discharges: methodological progress, clinical evaluation, and neurodevelopmental context.
papers.abstract: Interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) are established electroencephalographic biomarkers that support epilepsy diagnosis and characterization, but their visual identification is time-consuming and subject to inter-rater variability. This review critically examines automated IED analysis from rule-based systems to contemporary deep learning, with particular attention to task definition, validation design, and clinical workflow. We use the term "accuracy paradox" as an author-defined descriptive label-not as an established field-wide concept-for the mismatch between high performance on prese
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This review surveys automated methods for detecting interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) in EEG, tracing the evolution from rule-based systems to modern deep learning approaches. It emphasizes how task definition and validation design affect reported performance, and introduces the author-defined 'accuracy paradox' to describe mismatches between high benchmark scores and real-world clinical utility. The paper also discusses the neurodevelopmental context relevant to IED interpretation.

papers.title: Integrated single cell transcriptomics analysis for unraveling heterogeneity and plasticity of root cells for sustainable and regenerative agriculture.
papers.abstract: The plant root system architecture (RSA) functions in anchorage, acquisition of water and mineral nutrients, and exhibits pronounced phenotypic plasticity in response to the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of the soil environment. Resolving the regulatory networks that underpin root development is therefore a prerequisite for improving stress tolerance and yield. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) resolves transcriptional landscapes at cellular resolution, discriminating root zonation, lineage trajectories and cell-type-restricted responses to environmental signals. Coupling scRNA-seq to epig
papers.summary: This review discusses how single-cell RNA sequencing can be used to dissect the cellular heterogeneity and developmental plasticity of plant root systems, which are critical for nutrient uptake and stress tolerance. It highlights how coupling scRNA-seq with epigenomic profiling can reveal the regulatory networks controlling root cell identity and environmental responses, with implications for breeding crops with improved root architecture.

papers.title: Dynamic orchestration of structural and immune cells in acute Pseudomonas aeruginosa pneumonia revealed by time-resolved single-cell and spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa pneumonia triggers a complex, dynamic host response, yet the cellular coordination of inflammation and repair remains poorly defined.
papers.summary: This study uses time-resolved single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to map how structural and immune cells coordinate their responses during acute Pseudomonas aeruginosa pneumonia. The authors reveal dynamic cellular interactions underlying both inflammation and tissue repair, providing a detailed temporal atlas of the host response to this infection.

papers.title: Unraveling tumor cell heterogeneity and epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity in gastric adenocarcinoma: an integrative multi-omics framework evaluating PVR/CD155 as a tumor cell-intrinsic EMT-associated target.
papers.abstract: The tumor microenvironment (TME) of gastric adenocarcinoma is exceptionally heterogeneous, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a central mechanism promoting local invasion and metastatic spread. Even so, how EMT-programmed cells are spatially arranged within tumor tissue, how they interact with neighboring immune populations, and which molecular nodes might be exploited therapeutically remain incompletely defined.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to characterize tumor cell heterogeneity and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) programs in gastric adenocarcinoma, examining how EMT-programmed cells are spatially organized and interact with immune cells in the tumor microenvironment. The authors identify PVR/CD155 as a tumor cell-intrinsic EMT-associated molecule that could serve as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Single-cell lineage tracing in tumor organoids identifies expansion states depicting the origin and progression of lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Only a subset of epithelial cells can initiate progressive lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), yet the founder cell states that confer this competence remain poorly defined.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell lineage tracing in tumor organoids to identify specific expansion states of epithelial cells that can initiate lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). The findings suggest that only certain founder cell states are competent to drive tumor progression, offering new insights into the cellular origins of LUAD.

papers.title: A parallel convolution attention network for crop genomic prediction.
papers.abstract: Genome prediction is a breeding strategy that predicts crop phenotype through genomic markers. Traditional statistical models cannot accurately capture the complex relationships between genotypes and phenotypes, and deep neural networks have shown significant advantages in capturing nonlinear relationships. Deep learning methods in genome selection primarily utilize sequential convolutional kernels, which can lead to challenges such as gradient disappearance and computational inefficiency. In this study a novel crop genomic prediction method based on a parallel convolutional attention network
papers.summary: The authors introduce a parallel convolutional attention network for genomic prediction in crops, aiming to better capture nonlinear genotype-phenotype relationships than traditional statistical models and sequential convolutional deep learning approaches. The parallel convolution design is intended to mitigate gradient vanishing and improve computational efficiency for genome selection in breeding.

papers.title: Engineered Exosomal miRNAs for Post-Stroke Neural Repair: Mechanisms, Delivery Strategies, and Translational Challenges.
papers.abstract: Functional neurological recovery after ischemic stroke remains a formidable challenge in neuroscience. Exosomes serve as pivotal mediators of intercellular communication, and the microRNAs (miRNAs) they carry, in particular, offer a promising "cell-free therapy" strategy for promoting neurological repair. This review systematically summarizes the multi-target mechanisms by which exosomal miRNAs regulate the neurovascular unit (NVU) and outlines technical strategies to enhance exosomal therapeutic efficacy through targeted modification and engineered cargo loading, with the aim of constructing
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how exosomal microRNAs regulate the neurovascular unit after ischemic stroke and could serve as a cell-free therapy for neural repair. It also surveys engineering strategies—such as targeted modification and engineered cargo loading—to improve exosome delivery and therapeutic efficacy, while outlining translational barriers.

papers.title: Spatial multi-omics decoding of the fracture nonunion niche: from immune-vascular-skeletal crosstalk to precision regeneration.
papers.abstract: Fracture nonunion - the failure of bone to heal without surgical intervention - affects 5%-10% of all fractures and represents a substantial clinical and economic burden. Despite decades of research, the cellular and molecular mechanisms that distinguish successful repair from nonunion remain incompletely understood, largely because the fracture niche is a spatially organized, multicellular ecosystem whose crosstalk cannot be captured by bulk analyses. The recent convergence of spatial transcriptomics, single-cell multi-omics, spatial proteomics, and computational integration methods has opene
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial multi-omics technologies (spatial transcriptomics, single-cell multi-omics, spatial proteomics) can decode the cellular and molecular ecosystem of fracture nonunion, a condition affecting 5-10% of fractures. It emphasizes that the spatially organized immune-vascular-skeletal crosstalk underlying failed bone healing cannot be captured by bulk analyses, and highlights computational integration approaches for precision regeneration strategies.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell analysis characterizes malignant epithelial programs and context-dependent immune associations of MP7/SERINC2 in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) comprises heterogeneous malignant epithelial states, but it remains unclear which transcriptional programs recur across patients and how these programs relate to the immune context.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated single-cell analysis to identify recurrent malignant epithelial transcriptional programs in colorectal cancer and examines how these programs relate to immune context. It specifically highlights MP7/SERINC2 as a program with context-dependent immune associations, suggesting its role varies across tumor microenvironments.
